claim: mCherry was inserted into titin's exon 28 (Z-disk) via a targeting vector using homologous recombination in ES cells.
source: The mCherry cDNA was inserted into titin's exon 28 (Z-disk) via a targeting vector (Figure 1) using standard procedures (Radke et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation method with citation to established procedures.

claim: Homozygous and heterozygous Ttn(Z)-mCherry mice assembled functional sarcomeres.

evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: There was no obvious adverse phenotype in Ttn(Z)-mCherry mice.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements and comparison to previous models.

claim: There was no difference in heart-to-bodyweight ratio in Ttn(Z)-mCherry mice.

claim: There was no change in titin isoform expression in Ttn(Z)-mCherry mice.

claim: The mCherry fluorophore properly co-localizes with the Z-disk protein α-actinin in homozygous Ttn(Z)-mCherry mice.

claim: Ttn(Z)-mCherry has increased signal intensity compared with Ttn(Z)-dsRed mice.

claim: The fluorescent signal of Ttn(Z)-mCherry is stable over 14 hours with minor changes.
source: Stability of the fluorescent signal with minor changes over 14 hr and higher intensity of the mCherry signal measured in three cells (n = 3) as the average signal at three Z-disks.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data over 14 hours.

claim: The difference in signal intensity between mCherry and dsRed is significant with p<0.001 for all time points.
source: Difference is significant with p<0.001 for all time points, tested by two-way ANOVA.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of fluorescence intensity measurements.

claim: Titin is not a static backbone, but dynamically exchanged in the sarcomere within hours.
source: Measurements of titin kinetics in cardiomyocytes revealed that titin is not a static backbone, but dynamically exchanged in the sarcomere within hours with a faster exchange rate at its Z-disk region (da Silva Lopes et al., 2011; Rudolph et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by previous studies on titin kinetics in cardiomyocytes.

claim: Titin has a faster exchange rate at its Z-disk region compared to other regions.
source: Measurements of titin kinetics in cardiomyocytes revealed that titin is not a static backbone, but dynamically exchanged in the sarcomere within hours with a faster exchange rate at its Z-disk region (da Silva Lopes et al., 2011; Rudolph et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by previous kinetic studies.

claim: The Ttn(Z)-mCherry signal reemerges after 1 hour in FRAP experiments.

evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data and line profile analysis.

claim: The Ttn(M)-eGFP signal reemerges after 4 hours in FRAP experiments.

claim: The striated signal pattern did not recover in fixed cells during FRAP experiments.

claim: Only minimal background fluorescence was recovered in fixed cells after 14 hours.

claim: There was no difference in background fluorescence recovery between Ttn(Z)-mCherry and Ttn(M)-eGFP in fixed cells.

claim: The exchange half-life of Ttn(M)-eGFP is 4.9 hours.

claim: The exchange half-life of Ttn(Z)-mCherry is significantly reduced compared to Ttn(M)-eGFP.
